title: Hidden modal structure from trajectories alone; integral formulation rescues the high-noise regime
domain: equation discovery / linear dynamics / robust identification
problem: (a) Does a discovered model carry hidden analytic structure -- specifically, do normal modes fall out of trajectories that never mention them? (b) Can the documented derivative-form failure at sigma=0.05 be rescued without changing the discovery criterion?
hypothesis: (a) Linear sparse regression on coupled-oscillator trajectories yields A whose eigenfrequencies/mode-shapes match analytics to ~1e-12 clean and generalize to unseen ICs. (b) Regressing window-integrated states against integrated library values (never differentiating noisy states) substantially raises recovery at sigma=0.05.
baseline: Textbook modal analysis of known A (ground truth); derivative STLSQ from exp02 as the failing baseline for exp13.
proposed_improvement: No method novelty claimed (integral/weak forms exist in literature). Contributions: exact hidden-eigenstructure demonstration + measured derivative-vs-integral crossover with an honest correlated-residual caveat (THEORY P12).

experimental_evidence.result: |A-A*|=7.8e-12, eigfreq err 7.5e-13, mode-shape err 4.7e-13, holdout traj 4.4e-10; sigma=0.01: all <=1.5e-3

experimental_evidence.what: integral vs derivative at high noise
experimental_evidence.result: sigma=0.05: recovery 63% vs 7%, median rollout 0.031 vs 0.379; sigma=0.02: tie 0.53/0.53

novelty_notes: Both ingredients are folklore/literature-known (weak-form integration; modal analysis); packaged demonstrations with preregistered endpoints are incremental (audit 2026-08-26).
